moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
learningObjectives: Explain independent SaaS design and review Blueprint proposals
Define application context, Case Life Cycles, fields and Personas
Distinguish PDF reference from the .blueprint import file
Review import choices and post-import work in Pega Platform

elements.description: Blueprint combines templates and generative AI to propose application workflows. Stakeholders review and refine the proposed design before implementation.
Blueprint is SaaS, separate from a Pega Platform development instance and Operator login. Follow the SaaS service’s sign-in and collaboration access requirements.
Blueprint helps teams start design; the implementation team uses App Studio and Dev Studio after import to configure, test and extend the application.

elements.text: Blueprint is a collaborative draft plan. Review it with stakeholders, then use the import file as a starting point for implementation. The draft does not guarantee production readiness or a fixed delivery time.

bulletPoints: Start with a relevant industry template or a GenAI proposal; validate it against the organization’s requirements.
A Platform development instance is not required to start design; SaaS access still applies.

elements.description: Choose industry, sub-industry and department, or Other with a detailed functional description. Select a template or GenAI, provide organization and language details, and add supporting requirements assets.

Review and edit Case Types, Primary/Alternate Stages, Processes and Steps. Use Notes to capture routing, SLA and conditions; Preview my app helps review flow. Check data field types, descriptions, primary fields, single/multiple values and user-input/calculated sources.

Templates provide a starting design that still needs review. Validate Personas, access needs, Channels and release effort, then check the summary for workflow, Data Model and integration completeness.

elements.text: Generating a Blueprint is like giving a skilled drafter a paragraph about your business: they hand back a labeled floor plan (Case Types, Life Cycles, Data Model, Personas) that you then mark up together until it's right.

bulletPoints: Refine the proposed workflow, data and Personas with stakeholders before import.
Use PDF for reference and the technical .blueprint file for import; revision history supports later edits.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Importing a Pega Blueprint into Pega Platform

elements.description: Download the technical .blueprint file and a PDF reference. In App Studio, create an application with Build from a Blueprint, upload the technical file and review its details and built-on stack. An existing application must be saved as a template to use it through this New Application wizard.
The authorized implementation team performs import and configuration. Project responsibilities can assign an LSA; the source does not require an exclusive LSA permission.

In the documented new-application workflow, created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch. The exception concerns branch placement, not whether Access Roles are created. Base Rulesets are locked and merges require the appropriate password.
Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import Pega Blueprints into a new or existing application.

elements.text: Think of the Branch as a review area for generated rules. Access Roles are placed outside it; their location alone does not tell you whether they were created.

elements.description: Inheritance creates a new Case Type or data object based on one in the built-on application. Reusing a data object links to the existing built-on object without its own class in the new app. Skip a proposed asset when it does not fit the business design.

Check existing-app overlaps, merge the appropriate branch Rules, and refine Decision shapes, Flow Actions, locking and the Data Model. Review database mapping, Data Pages and properties, and test approvals, alternate paths, automation and child Cases.

bulletPoints: Choose build/inherit/skip for Case Types and build/inherit/reuse/skip for data objects; build or skip Personas.
Check class layers and Case/data classes before Submit, then inspect and refine the result.
PremBridge is not required. Review branch placement and configure security, data and integration needs.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Using Blueprint for an Industry App (Customer Service for Insurance)

elements.description: In the insurance example, start from the Customer Service template and add a golf-cart Case. Inherit existing Case Types and build the new one. Add a weather Step and field; after import, change the field to Picklist and add it to a View. Configure data, integrations, Channels and users, then simulate an interaction.

elements.text: Industry templates are pre-fab housing kits: instead of designing an insurance service app from scratch, you start from a kit tuned for that industry and customize the rooms (Case Types/workflows).

bulletPoints: An industry template provides a starting point; the team still reviews and configures it.
The insurance example includes workflow and data changes before and after import.

examPitfalls.title: Independent SaaS still has access controls
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Independence from a Platform Operator login is not a promise of anonymous Blueprint SaaS access.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check service sign-in and collaboration permissions separately from the target Platform instance.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint augments, not replaces, App Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Distractors claim Blueprint replaces App Studio/Dev Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Blueprint augments existing tools by accelerating design; you still build/refine in App Studio.

examPitfalls.title: What Blueprint proposes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The proposal set is tested: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Blueprint drafts the app skeleton (workflow + data + personas), not infrastructure or production integrations.

examPitfalls.title: Who imports the Blueprint
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The team assigns an authorized implementation owner; the source does not state a universal LSA-only import permission.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Agree project responsibility and verify target environment access.

examPitfalls.title: Import creates assets in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles
examPitfalls.trapDescription: For the documented new-application workflow, Access Roles are outside the Branch. This does not mean they are absent from the application.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Differentiate branch placement from asset creation.

examPitfalls.title: PremBridge is not required to import
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume PremBridge is a prerequisite for Blueprint import.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import a Blueprint into a new or existing application.

examPitfalls.title: Import target can be new OR existing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Extending an existing app can introduce overlaps. The New Application wizard requires a saved existing-app template when building on that application.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review built-on inheritance and reuse choices.

examPitfalls.title: Best-practice templates value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Templates are an industry starting point, not a guarantee of zero technical debt or production readiness.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review and test the generated configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team without access to a Pega Platform development instance wants to start Blueprint design. What makes that possible?

options.text: Blueprint is separate SaaS; Platform instance access is not required to start the proposal
It runs only inside Dev Studio
It requires every participant to have an LSA license
It can only be used after the app is already built

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate Platform access from Blueprint service access.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint is independent of a Platform development instance and Operator login. This does not imply anonymous or unrestricted access to the SaaS service.

optionExplanations.A: The design service can be used before provisioning the target Platform instance.
optionExplanations.B: Dev Studio is not where the standalone design service runs.
optionExplanations.C: Participation is not restricted to architects with this license.
optionExplanations.D: Early design is one of the purposes of Blueprint.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After you describe an application in business terms, what does Blueprint propose?

options.text: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas
Server hardware and network topology
Only a list of Rulesets
Only Access Roles

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint uses AI to draft the application skeleton — Case Types, Data Models, and Personas.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas, which you then refine. It does not propose infrastructure or only Rulesets/Access Roles.

optionExplanations.A: These proposals describe the business application rather than infrastructure.
optionExplanations.B: Hardware topology is outside the application-design proposal.
optionExplanations.C: Ruleset packaging alone does not describe the proposed workflow.
optionExplanations.D: Access roles alone do not represent the cases and data design.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A project manager asks whether importing a Pega Blueprint means the team no longer needs App Studio for ongoing development. Which statement about Blueprint's relationship to App Studio is correct?

options.text: Blueprint augments App Studio and other Pega tools; it does not replace them
Blueprint replaces App Studio entirely
Blueprint is a feature inside Admin Studio
Blueprint and App Studio cannot be used on the same project

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint augments App Studio without replacing it; the two tools work together in sequence.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint augments existing Pega tools by accelerating design; you still build and refine in App Studio. It is not a replacement and is not part of Admin Studio.

optionExplanations.A: The imported starting point still needs studio-based refinement.
optionExplanations.B: Import does not remove the need to implement and configure behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Admin Studio monitors runtime rather than host Blueprint design.
optionExplanations.D: A project can use Blueprint designs and App Studio together.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A project assigns its LSA responsibility for importing the reviewed Blueprint. Who performs this work in the scenario?

options.text: The Lead System Architect (LSA), as the assigned implementation owner
The Product Owner
The Scrum Master
The end customer

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the explicit project assignment rather than a universal role rule.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This team assigned the LSA to technical implementation. The source does not impose an exclusive LSA-only import permission.

optionExplanations.A: The LSA is explicitly assigned this project’s import work.
optionExplanations.B: The Product Owner prioritizes scope rather than own this technical task.
optionExplanations.C: The Scrum Master facilitates delivery rather than own application import.
optionExplanations.D: The customer supplies requirements rather than perform this architect responsibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented new-application Blueprint import, which created asset is the exception to Branch placement?

options.text: Access Roles
Case Types
Data objects
Personas

practiceQuiz.hint: One specific asset type is NOT placed in the Branch during a Blueprint import — it relates to security.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Access Roles are outside the Branch in this new-application workflow. That placement exception does not imply they were not created.

optionExplanations.A: Access Roles are the exception to branch placement, not necessarily to creation.
optionExplanations.B: Case Types are created within the branch for review.
optionExplanations.C: Data objects belong to the branch-created assets.
optionExplanations.D: Personas are among the assets created within the branch.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team believes they must install Pega GenAI PremBridge before they can import a Blueprint. Is this correct?

options.text: No — PremBridge is not required to import a Blueprint into a new or existing application
Yes — PremBridge is mandatory for all imports
Yes — but only for existing applications
No — but the Blueprint cannot target an existing application

practiceQuiz.hint: PremBridge is NOT a prerequisite; Blueprint imports can target a new or an existing application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The cited import workflow does not require PremBridge for a new or existing application. The target environment still needs appropriate configuration and access.

optionExplanations.A: The import path does not require this GenAI bridge.
optionExplanations.B: The stated import process works without mandatory PremBridge installation.
optionExplanations.C: Existing-application import is not the stated exception requiring PremBridge.
optionExplanations.D: Blueprint supports an existing target as well as a new application.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the primary value of importing a Blueprint into Pega Platform?

options.text: It accelerates creation of an editable starting application for demos and further configuration
It permanently locks the application to Blueprint
It deletes existing Case Types
It disables App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: The import provides a starting point for implementation and review.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Blueprint import jumpstarts development and demonstrations; the team must still configure and test the application. A fixed creation time is not guaranteed.

optionExplanations.A: It supplies a starting application, with further refinement still needed.
optionExplanations.B: The resulting application can continue evolving in the studios.
optionExplanations.C: Import is not described as indiscriminate case deletion.
optionExplanations.D: App Studio remains available for implementation and refinement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA team is about to generate their first Blueprint for a claims application and wants to understand the process. Which TWO statements correctly describe how generating and modifying a Blueprint works?

options.text: You describe the app in business terms and Blueprint proposes an initial design
You refine the proposal (Stages, Steps, fields, data objects, Personas) before importing
Once generated, a Blueprint cannot be edited
Generation requires writing Java code

practiceQuiz.hint: The Blueprint workflow follows: describe → AI proposes → team refines → export/import into Pega.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes an initial design from a business-terms description, and you refine it collaboratively before import. Blueprints are editable and require no Java. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: Business context seeds the initial proposal.
optionExplanations.B: Human refinement aligns the proposal with the actual requirements.
optionExplanations.D: The design workflow does not require Java authoring.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants to stand up a Customer Service for Insurance application quickly while following Pega best practices. How does Blueprint help?

options.text: It provides industry best-practice templates to start from, which the team refines for their needs
It forbids any customization of the generated design
It only works for generic, non-industry apps
It requires rebuilding all Case Types by hand first

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint includes industry-specific templates to accelerate design for common business domains.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint offers best-practice and industry-specific templates to accelerate design; teams refine the AI proposal before importing it. Blueprint supports customization and industry scenarios, not just generic processes.

optionExplanations.A: Industry templates provide a starting point to adapt.
optionExplanations.B: Requirements-specific refinement is part of the workflow.
optionExplanations.D: Rebuilding everything first would negate the design accelerator's value.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why did Pega create Blueprint, given that traditional application design took weeks to months?

options.text: Its GenAI-infused approach helps teams align on an optimized solution and reach development faster
To remove the need for any business stakeholder input
To replace the Case Life Cycle concept
To store production data

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint speeds stakeholder alignment during design, reducing time before development can begin.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint's generative-AI approach helps teams align on an optimized design and get into development faster than the slow traditional process. It increases (not removes) stakeholder collaboration.

optionExplanations.A: Early proposals help stakeholders agree before implementation.
optionExplanations.B: Stakeholders must review the proposed business design.
optionExplanations.C: Cases and their lifecycles remain central to the proposal.
optionExplanations.D: Blueprint is a design tool rather than a production record store.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA wants to create a new Blueprint for an upcoming project but is unsure which tool or platform to open. Where should they navigate to create a Pega Blueprint?

options.text: pega.com/blueprint
Admin Studio
Prediction Studio
The Records tab in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint is accessed at a specific standalone SaaS web address (pega.com/blueprint).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint is created and accessed at pega.com/blueprint, reflecting its standalone SaaS nature — it is not embedded in Admin Studio, Prediction Studio, or the Records tab.

optionExplanations.A: The separate Blueprint site is the design entry point.
optionExplanations.B: Runtime administration is unrelated to creating this Blueprint.
optionExplanations.C: Analytical model management is a different studio responsibility.
optionExplanations.D: The standalone service is not an App Studio Records tab.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team uses the documented new-application Build from a Blueprint workflow. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: An existing application can be used as the built-on app after saving it as a template
Created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch; this is a placement exception
Import always overwrites the entire production database
Only the BA can import a Blueprint

practiceQuiz.hint: Check the wizard’s template requirement and branch-placement exception.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The wizard requires saving an existing application as a template for the built-on stack. Access Roles are outside the Branch in the documented new-application workflow.

optionExplanations.A: Save an existing app as a template to use it in this New Application wizard.
optionExplanations.B: The source describes a placement exception, not exclusion from asset creation.
optionExplanations.C: Application-design import is not a full database overwrite.
optionExplanations.D: Import is not restricted to the BA who designed the proposal.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is presenting the Pega Blueprint workflow to new project team members who have never worked with AI-assisted design before. Which option best captures the correct end-to-end Blueprint flow?

options.text: Describe in business terms → Blueprint proposes design → refine collaboratively → export and import into Pega to jumpstart the build
Write Java → compile → deploy
Open Admin Studio → monitor system → restart
Create Access Roles → lock Rulesets → publish

practiceQuiz.hint: The Blueprint process is: describe the business → AI proposes → refine → import to jumpstart build.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Blueprint workflow is: describe the application in business terms → AI proposes the design → the team refines → export or import into Pega Platform to jumpstart development. The other options describe unrelated activities.

optionExplanations.A: The sequence includes both proposal review and application import.
optionExplanations.B: Java compilation omits the business-design collaboration described here.
optionExplanations.C: Runtime monitoring is not the Blueprint generation workflow.
optionExplanations.D: Role creation and ruleset locking do not generate a business design.

quickRecap.value: Separate SaaS design service, independent of a Platform instance/Operator login; follow SaaS access rules.
Augments App Studio and other tools — does not replace them; applies decades of best practices via templates.
From a business-terms description: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas — then refined collaboratively.
Use the technical .blueprint file in the New Application wizard, review import choices and continue configuration and testing.
In the documented new-application flow, created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch; this describes placement.
NOT required to import a Blueprint.
Start from industry best-practice templates (e.g., Customer Service for Insurance) and refine for the organization.
